races.name: Wakefield Thornes Cricket Club Nursery

runners_data.name: Poppy Foxy
runners_data.note: Rated OR 65 and the race's lone front-runner, she gets to control tempo entirely unchallenged which is a significant tactical advantage; Kieran Shoemark is an upgrade in the saddle and her two runs on Good ground are relevant, though she needs to reproduce better than her latest fifth to score.

runners_data.name: Claret And Blues
runners_data.note: Unknown style horse who is likely to slot prominently just behind the leader, giving her an ideal position in this slowly-run affair; Warren Fentiman's claim is useful and she has placed form on Good ground, though a 38-day break is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Fasthope
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who gets his preferred running position at the rear legitimately in this field; Cam Hardie is an experienced northern claimer and Fasthope's only similar-going start ended in a third, though a closing run from off a slow pace is a genuine concern.

runners_data.name: Priscilla's Hope
runners_data.note: A hold-up type who has placed twice in similar conditions and shows consistency in her form string — her best chance comes if the pace is genuinely strong enough to reel in, which on current evidence looks optimistic given Poppy Foxy's likely control.

runners_data.name: Baila Morena
runners_data.note: Recent form reads 7-4-0 and is heading the wrong way; her true preference is for a strong pace to aim at, but this race is unlikely to supply it, and with Ollie Pears's yard at 0 from 6 over 14 days there is limited confidence in an upturn here.

runners_data.name: Black Cuillin
runners_data.note: Two runs in, both finishing fourth on Good ground, suggesting a consistent but limited profile; a genuine hold-up racer who has been placed into midfield by the volume of similar types in this field, meaning she races slightly out of role and must find improvement to figure.

runners_data.name: Givendale
runners_data.note: Carries a fading-in-finish flag from recent data and that tendency is particularly damaging in a race where a slow pace removes the late momentum hold-up horses depend on; Alex Jary's claim doesn't outweigh concerns about her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Mary
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated runner at OR 45 with a form string of 9-7-4 and inconsistent finishes; Andrew Mullen keeps the ride for Ben Haslam but 41 days off and a deteriorating profile make it hard to build a case, even with her hold-up style being natural rather than forced.

races.paceDynamic: Poppy Foxy is the only confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure her, she is expected to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over Pontefract's straight six furlongs on Good ground. Claret And Blues has an unknown style but is likely to sit just behind, meaning Poppy Foxy effectively dictates terms unchallenged and controls tempo throughout. The remainder of the field — Fasthope, Priscilla's Hope, Baila Morena, Black Cuillin, Givendale and Spirit Of Mary — are all hold-up types in their natural role, but this field holds more genuine hold-up horses than the race map can place at the rear, meaning Baila Morena, Black Cuillin, Givendale and Spirit Of Mary are redistributed to midfield despite preferring to come from off the pace. A steady, uncontested pace set by a lone front-runner strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and sustain their effort to the line — hold-up horses mapped to mid-pack are unlikely to find the late sprint they need when the gallop has not been truly strong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Poppy Foxy Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Poppy Foxy bowls along uncontested at a comfortable tempo and the field fails to generate a strong enough closing surge.
scenarios.body: Poppy Foxy dictates a controlled pace, conserving energy for the final two furlongs, and her rivals — most of whom prefer a stronger gallop to aim at — find the deficit too great to bridge on a track that rewards those up with the pace. Prominent types who slot in directly behind benefit most, as they travel within the race and need only sustain rather than accelerate from distance.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaser Runs Over
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracking Poppy Foxy just off the pace proves stronger in the final furlong and swamps the leader close home.
scenarios.body: Claret And Blues or Priscilla's Hope, sitting comfortably in the slipstream, preserves energy through the controlled fractions and finds a decisive gear in the closing stages to head the front-runner. Pontefract's straight six is fair to both front-runners and closers when the pace is moderate, keeping this scenario live.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and midfield horses — true hold-up types pushed forward — manage to find gaps and pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: With much of the midfield filled by naturally hold-up horses racing out of role, any sustained late swoop requires them to find more than their redistribution to midfield allows, making this scenario distinctly less likely. Fasthope, who has the best recent form of the hold-up group, is the most plausible beneficiary if it does materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Bunching Intervenes
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems, a stumble, or a fractious start disrupts normal race order and reshapes the contest entirely.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up horses crowded into the middle of the field, there is a meaningful risk of interference or crowding that could shuffle form unexpectedly in the straight. In such a scramble, horses with experienced jockeys or established course form would hold an edge, though this scenario remains unlikely on Good ground with a clear leader.

watchPoints.text: Poppy Foxy — if she breaks cleanly and establishes her lead by the two-furlong marker uncontested, she is the primary danger to all as the only horse guaranteed to get her preferred position in this race.

Claret And Blues — watch the early pace she shows leaving the stalls; if she pushes forward to track the leader she is ideally placed, but her unknown style tag means an unexpected hold-up ride could waste her chance entirely.

Baila Morena and Black Cuillin — both true hold-up horses crowded into midfield; if they interfere with each other or with Fasthope in the early stages, traffic issues could compromise multiple runners simultaneously.

Givendale — her flagged tendency to fade in the finish combined with a slow pace and an out-of-role midfield position makes her a horse to oppose rather than support, and could drag down those immediately around her if she weakens abruptly.

Priscilla's Hope — the one hold-up type with a recent placed run on similar going; worth monitoring in running to see if Rowan Scott opts to push her forward early, as a prominent position would materially improve her prospects in this shape.

races.name: Noel John Curtin Memorial Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Hellion
runners_data.note: Off a 297-day absence and stepping back to 10 furlongs having run exclusively at 16f recently, this four-year-old drops markedly in trip; John Donald McCain's yard is 2/12 in the last 14 days and the horse's natural rear-of-field style means it will not be travelling in its comfort zone if pushed forward by the congested hold-up group.

runners_data.name: Sixty Plus
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with the most course-and-distance exposure of any runner here, but recent form over 12-24 furlongs on Soft and Good shows mid-field finishes rather than wins; Joanna Mason rides and the horse needs a pace to develop to deploy its finishing effort, which this race shape may not provide.

runners_data.name: Tiernan
runners_data.note: Has placed twice at 11 furlongs on Good for Iain Jardine and Paul Mulrennan but also posted a poor 22nd at Haydock; naturally a hold-up horse whose map position overstates its likely berth in this race, and 38 days off since its last run is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Freddy Fearless
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old with a single outing — fourth over 8f on Good — and an unclassified style leaving tactical options open for William Pyle; David and Nicola Barron's yard is 2/9 in the last 14 days and the extra four furlongs here is an unknown quantity.

runners_data.name: Kinetic Impact
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes the mount for Charles Hills on this lightly raced colt who has placed third in both starts over 10 furlongs on Good ground, giving it the most directly relevant form profile in the race; unclassified style means it could slot into a prominent position if the pace is slow, which would be ideal.

runners_data.name: Moon Zabeel
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston-trained three-year-old with a single run — sixth over 12 furlongs on Good — and a natural hold-up preference that places it in the rear group, though the volume of closers in this field means it is likely pushed closer to midfield than it would naturally choose; only 19 days since last run.

runners_data.name: Steel Raven
runners_data.note: Two runs for Adrian Paul Keatley, both thirds — once on Good, once on Soft — suggest consistency without a win; unclassified style with a recent run six days ago, and the step up to 10 furlongs for the first time is untested, though the placed form on cut ground shows it handles variety.

runners_data.name: Khepri
runners_data.note: K R Burke has the yard firing at 9/53 over 14 days and Clifford Lee takes the ride, but this three-year-old has only one run to its name — fourth over 10 furlongs on Good — and its natural inclination to race in the rear will be compromised by the sheer number of hold-up horses in this field.

runners_data.name: Talitha Rouge
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope is a key booking for David O'Meara and this filly has placed in both starts — third and fourth over 10-12 furlongs on Good — with the most directly relevant form over this exact surface and trip combination; a natural hold-up profile, but should be able to secure a good position given it is not flagged for redistribution.

runners_data.name: Twin And Tonic
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's three-year-old has a single run — 11th over 7 furlongs on Good — which is the least informative piece of form in the field given the distance step from sprint to 1m2f; flagged for fading finishes and with Oisin McSweeney aboard, this is the most speculative entry in the race.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 1m2f Pontefract maiden is set to be tactically cautious early, with the majority of the 10 runners — Hellion, Sixty Plus, Tiernan, Moon Zabeel, Khepri, Talitha Rouge, and Twin And Tonic — all natural hold-up or prominent types, leaving the pace to fall to the unexposed youngsters Freddy Fearless, Kinetic Impact, and Steel Raven, none of whom have shown reliable front-running tendencies. The result is likely to be a falsely-run, dawdling affair through the early stages before the pace quickens sharply in the straight, compressing the field and reducing the advantage for any horse that tries to make it a genuine stamina test. Pontefract's undulating, turning track amplifies the danger of getting caught wide or racing too keenly when the field bunches, making positioning off the slow pace critical. This race shape strongly favours horses with a prominent-to-midfield profile who can sit handy without being exposed on the front end, travel comfortably into the straight, and quicken over the final two furlongs — the field holds more hold-up types than can all get their natural rear position, and Hellion, Moon Zabeel, and Khepri are the most likely to be pushed forward out of their usual roles, meaning true closers firing late from the back may find little reward.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field drifts through the early stages at a crawl and the race becomes a two-furlong dash from the home turn.
scenarios.body: The lack of a genuine front-runner means the tempo is almost certain to compress into a sprint finish, suiting those who can quicken sharply from a handy position rather than those grinding from behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced three-year-olds — Kinetic Impact, Freddy Fearless, or Steel Raven — edges forward to control a modest gallop and holds on in the straight.
scenarios.body: A horse that settles in front at a comfortable tempo on Good ground at Pontefract can be very hard to peg back when nothing has the pace to reel them in late; Kinetic Impact's two outings over 10 furlongs on Good give it the clearest stamina profile for this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion at the back resolves cleanly and one of the naturally hold-up horses — Talitha Rouge or Sixty Plus — finds a clear run from mid-race to challenge in the straight.
scenarios.body: Talitha Rouge has shown progressive form over 10-12 furlongs on Good ground with Daniel Tudhope in the plate, giving it a strong surface-and-trip fit; Sixty Plus brings the most course exposure but needs things to set up cleanly from off the pace, which is far from guaranteed here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Catches Out Quickeners
scenarios.trigger: If, against expectation, a genuine pace develops early and the race turns into a true test of stamina over the full 1m2f.
scenarios.body: This scenario is the least likely given the absence of a confirmed front-runner, but if the pace does materialise, proven stayers with experience over the trip — Sixty Plus and Tiernan — would be best placed to grind past tiring rivals.

watchPoints.text: Kinetic Impact and Steel Raven are the only horses with an unclassified style who could drift to the front and control the pace — if either does so from stall, they could dictate terms in a field that has no natural front-runner to challenge them.

The four redistributed hold-up types — Hellion, Moon Zabeel, Khepri, and Tiernan — are all likely to be racing closer than ideal, creating potential for traffic problems and interference in the straight as they converge from an unnatural position.

Sixty Plus has the most mileage in the tank but needs a genuine pace to set up its finish; if the race drifts into a sprint as expected, its hold-up style becomes a liability rather than an asset and its chance diminishes sharply.

Twin And Tonic's only run was over 7 furlongs and ended in 11th — the step to 1m2f at Pontefract is a significant jump in trip and the finishing-fade flag makes it worth monitoring to see whether it is eased or pulled up if the race develops into a genuine test.

Talitha Rouge with Tudhope is the most natural hold-up runner not tagged for redistribution — watch where it settles in the first quarter-mile, as its ability to find a clean position in the rear group without being crowded out by the other closers will determine whether it can deliver its finishing run effectively.

races.name: Weatherbys Pipalong Stakes (Fillies' & Mares' Listed)

runners_data.name: Bellarchi
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here with five wins to her name, including back-to-back wins going into this race; style fit as front-runner is strong, but the [STYLE_FIT] flag suggests she is operating slightly outside a purely ideal shape — her form on Good is mixed (9th last time at this distance), yet she commands the rail role and her recent win record is hard to dismiss.

runners_data.name: American Gal
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's consistent performer has been knocking on the door without converting on Good ground, going 0W1P from 11 similar-going runs; she is a natural front-runner by inclination but this crowded prominent group has displaced her into a midfield mapping, meaning she is likely to race in a position that blunts her effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Arisaig
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston fields a mare with a fine consistent profile on Good ground — 14 runs, 0 wins but 5 places — and Pontefract's turning mile suits a horse happy to stalk at the head of affairs; Jamie Spencer is an astute handler of positional races and should slot her comfortably behind Bellarchi.

runners_data.name: Brazilian Rose
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies' mare steps up in class from recent handicap form and her last five starts are all at 6f-7f, making this 1m trip a stamina question mark; headgear noted (h) and limited form on Good ground (2 runs, no places) compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: Cheshire Dancer
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's five-year-old carries the headgear flag (p) and has solid course-distance experience with 2 wins from 12 similar-going runs; David Probert should get her to a prominent pitch, though her last run — 8th on Good over this trip — was uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Consecrated
runners_data.note: William Haggas sends out a hold-up horse whose last five runs are predominantly on Soft, with most of her better form coming at longer trips; Tom Marquand is a strong ally, but the genuine hold-up style here relies on a stronger pace than Bellarchi alone is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: Crystal Flyer
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's mare is a consistent hold-up type whose recent form reads poorly — 0W0P from 15 similar-going runs — and the trainer has a blank 14-day record (0/21); no obvious angle to suggest she can break through at Listed level from this profile.

runners_data.name: Goldilocks Cen
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's lightly-raced four-year-old has only three similar-going runs and an uncertain style (U-tagged), which makes her genuinely difficult to place in any pace scenario; Daniel Tudhope is a top booking and her 4th last season at 9f shows some staying ability, but the class rise is steep.

runners_data.name: Mobberley Rose
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's mare arrives on the back of two starts — a Listed second and a win — with a 55-day absence to account for; she is a genuine front-runner by nature but the overcrowded prominent group means she is mapped to midfield, a position that will frustrate her natural rhythm on returning from that layoff.

runners_data.name: Mostar Dreams
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's five-year-old has winning form on Good going at this sort of trip and comes in just 13 days after her last run; she races from a hold-up position but her better form has come on Soft/Standard surfaces, and the 8 similar-going runs yield 2 wins but suggest she needs things to fall right.

runners_data.name: Never Let Go
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's second string brings the highest win rate among the prominent horses at this trip on Good going (1W5P from 7 runs), and Kieran Shoemark should get a prominent berth ahead of the redistributed rivals; the 54-day absence is the only doubt, but she handled a similar break before a placed run last season.

runners_data.name: Radiant Beauty
runners_data.note: James Owen's mare has a strong record on Good ground — 2 wins, 3 places from 5 similar-going runs — and James Doyle is an obvious class booking; she is a natural front-runner by style but with the prominent berths oversubscribed she is mapped back into midfield, a position she has rarely been asked to race from and which may not suit her.

races.paceDynamic: Bellarchi is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with a clear lead role unchallenged, she is likely to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop around Pontefract's turning mile. The field is loaded with prominent-racing types — Arisaig, Brazilian Rose, Cheshire Dancer, Never Let Go, and redistributed American Gal, Radiant Beauty, and Mobberley Rose — meaning a scrappy battle for early position will compress the prominent group, with several of those mares forced to sit deeper than their natural style demands. Bellarchi can exploit the chaos behind her, rolling along at a fair but unspectacular pace that denies the true hold-up horses a sufficient velocity to aim at. This race shape strongly favours horses capable of tracking the leader in the first two or three positions and quickening from a clear sightline — true Prominent/Early Pace profiles who get their natural berth will be best placed, while genuine hold-up horses are at a structural disadvantage unless the pace accelerates markedly in the final quarter-mile. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race can accommodate at the head of affairs; Arisaig, Cheshire Dancer, and Never Let Go are best-positioned to actually secure prominent slots given their class and course-distance profiles, with American Gal, Radiant Beauty, and Mobberley Rose likely shuffled back against their wishes.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bellarchi Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Bellarchi leads unchallenged and sets a honest but not frenetic pace that rewards those tracking her in second or third.
scenarios.body: Bellarchi rolls along the front, and the horses who manage to slot in just behind her travel comfortably into the straight with running left; a prominent tracker quickens past a tiring leader in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On Under Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If the pace behind Bellarchi becomes fractious enough to hurt the prominent chasers, allowing the leader to steal a march she never surrenders.
scenarios.body: With the prominent group tangled in a positional battle, Bellarchi's momentum is never disrupted and she kicks clear turning in, holding on gamely to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to stretch the field and create a gap for a well-positioned midfield runner to cut through late.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting fourth to sixth early avoids the early friction, travels smoothly into the straight, and finds clear daylight to finish powerfully when others have used energy fighting for position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace quickens enough in the first half to string the field out and leave true hold-up horses with a target to aim at.
scenarios.body: The contested early gallop drains the leaders and prominent horses, and hold-up runners produce a sweeping late run from the back of the field down the Pontefract straight.

watchPoints.text: Bellarchi is the sole genuine front-runner in a 12-runner field and could exploit a clean lead if the prominent pack fractures behind her — watch whether she is allowed to dictate an uncontested pace into the straight.

Arisaig and Never Let Go are the prominent types best-equipped to seize the crucial second-or-third position; if either secures a clear sightline on Bellarchi turning in, they become the dominant threat in the most likely race shape.

Radiant Beauty, American Gal, and Mobberley Rose are all natural front-runners who may be squeezed for early position — a fractious first two furlongs among these three could burn energy across several runners and alter the pace dynamic unexpectedly.

Consecrated and Mostar Dreams are the two hold-up horses with any realistic winning claims, but their scenario depends on a pace strong enough to string the field — if Bellarchi dials it back, watch for both to be niggled along earlier than their jockeys would prefer.

Goldilocks Cen's unknown style tag under Daniel Tudhope is worth monitoring at the start — if she breaks forward and adds to the early pace rather than settling mid-division, it reshapes the race considerably.

races.name: Pontefract Park Silver Sprint Trophy Handicap

runners_data.name: The Strikin Viking
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 104 and a confirmed hold-up horse; won over course-relevant 6f on Soft last time before finishing 5th, and with 143 days off the freshness angle is worth noting — Good ground suits (OK tag), and Bughenaim rides for the same yard as Garfield Shadow which could create a tactical double act.|

runners_data.name: Garfield Shadow
runners_data.note: Off the track for 593 days — the fitness question is real and is the single biggest risk to this race's shape; when last seen he finished 1st and 3rd over 6f on Good, and James Doyle's booking for a yard recording 0 wins from 12 runners in 14 days adds caution, though his role as uncontested front-runner at least maximises his chance of lasting home.|

runners_data.name: El Bodon
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam sends this five-year-old out just 8 days after its last run — a quick turnaround that can be a positive signal — but its Good-ground form over 6f has been poor (0 wins, 0 places from 15 similar-going runs), and the p headgear may be doing a job that isn't translating in these conditions.|

runners_data.name: Dark Cloud Rising
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 6f Good-ground configuration last time and Tudhope takes the ride for O'Meara's yard which is 8 from 63 in 14 days — solid but not firing at top clip; the v headgear is retained and he has the profile of a horse who can genuinely hold a prominent position and sustain it, giving him a natural fit in this race shape.|

runners_data.name: Badri
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old veteran who has won twice over 6f on Good and is in the form of his life (1-7-1 in recent starts); his natural front-running instincts are the issue here — with Garfield Shadow ahead and Dark Cloud Rising also wanting to press, he may find himself unable to dominate as he prefers, and his style-fit discount (0.93) reflects a race shape that may blunt his best attributes.|

runners_data.name: Beaujolais Nouveau
runners_data.note: Won over 6f Good ground earlier in the season and Mullen partners him for Haslam's yard (1 from 16 in 14 days); his natural hold-up style means he's been mapped to midfield in this analysis because the field has more closers than the race shape can accommodate at the rear, and with a small field of six he may find himself too close to the pace too soon to deliver his best late kick.|

races.paceDynamic: Garfield Shadow is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is expected to stride clear from the gates and control a sustainable, even gallop over Pontefract's 6f on Good ground. Dark Cloud Rising and Badri are both naturally prominent types who will want to sit close to the pace, but with Garfield Shadow likely to dictate uncontested, the true pace scenario here is moderate rather than searching. The field holds more prominent types than can comfortably hold their natural position: Badri and Beaujolais Nouveau are genuine pace-pressing or hold-up horses who are likely to find themselves racing slightly off their preferred roles, with Dark Cloud Rising best placed of the chasers to actually secure the position directly behind Garfield Shadow. A lone front-runner dictating a fair but not brutal pace on Good ground at Pontefract favours horses who can travel prominently and sustain their effort through the final furlong — confirmed prominent racers with strong recent form and course-suitable profiles hold the clear tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls All
scenarios.trigger: If Garfield Shadow leads unchallenged and sets a sustainable pace that suits a prominent-to-midfield finisher.
scenarios.body: Garfield Shadow dictates from the front at a measured gallop, leaving the race to those travelling smoothly just off the pace; any horse able to peel off his flank in the straight takes the race before the hold-up runners can close. Dark Cloud Rising, fresh off a recent win and handled by Tudhope, is ideally placed to track and pounce, while Badri's genuine prominence gives it a chance to convert if it can get close to the pace it naturally wants.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collects Late Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Garfield Shadow's long absence (593 days) causes it to tire in the final furlong and open the race for hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: Should Garfield Shadow's race fitness betray it late, the pace collapses in the closing stages and a hold-up runner with a clean run can pick up the pieces; The Strikin Viking, a genuine hold-up horse with solid recent Good-ground form, is best positioned to capitalise on this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Duel Plays Into Hands
scenarios.trigger: If Dark Cloud Rising pushes up to challenge Garfield Shadow aggressively, creating a genuine early duel and forcing a stronger pace.
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop would stretch the small field and see the front two racing harder than ideal, opening the door for the hold-up horse The Strikin Viking who has the highest OR in the field and the tactical patience to arrive late; Badri would also be in contention if it can slot in third and benefit from the duel burning off those ahead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Upset From The Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and all prominent types empty late, allowing the deepest closers a rare winning opportunity at Pontefract.
scenarios.body: El Bodon, who carries a hold-up flag in its headgear history and was beaten only a length in a similar grade recently, could sweep through if the race truly falls apart in the straight; Beaujolais Nouveau, though mapped to midfield and racing out of its natural hold-up role, retains a win on Good ground and would factor only if unusually well positioned.

watchPoints.text: Garfield Shadow's 593-day absence is the race's pivotal risk — if he shows any sign of blowing up or not handling the fitness test through the final furlong, the entire pace scenario unravels and the race opens dramatically for The Strikin Viking and Dark Cloud Rising.

Badri has the form to win this but watch whether Jason Hart can secure a position close enough to the pace in the opening furlong — if Dark Cloud Rising and Garfield Shadow shut him out early, his prominent instincts will count for little and he will be racing in a role that doesn't suit him.

Dark Cloud Rising's headgear (visor) and recent course win make him the most interesting tactical watch — if Tudhope sends him forward aggressively to challenge Garfield Shadow, the pace quickens and the race becomes a different contest to the one the map predicts.

With only six runners and a controlled pace likely, draw and positioning in the opening two furlongs will be exaggerated — any horse slow from the gates risks being stranded in a small, compact field with no cover and no pace to aim at in the straight.

races.name: Pontefract Squash And Leisure Club Handicap

runners_data.name: Dubai Venture
runners_data.note: Best form comes over 12-13f on Good or Soft and two wins at 12f on Good ground are directly relevant here; a natural hold-up horse who needs cover and a strong gallop, and the thin pace from Clipsham Noble alone may not set this up ideally, though Joanna Mason's record in staying handicaps is solid.

runners_data.name: Lednikov
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran whose recent five runs have all been mid-division finishes between 5th and 7th, consistently finding little at the finish; blinkers likely sharpen focus but Good ground form is modest (0W2P in 15 similar-going runs) and the 14-day turnaround with Furtado's 1/34 recent strike rate is uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Jedhi Knight
runners_data.note: Ran in 16f and 17f races on Soft last time out — dropping back to 14f on Good is a meaningful change in conditions, and his best efforts were on softer ground; David Nolan's booking is a positive, but two of his last three runs were at distances longer than today's trip and on going considerably softer.

runners_data.name: Clipsham Noble
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the race and likely to stride clear unchallenged from flag to flag; won over 12f on Good at Pontefract recently which is directly applicable, though a style-fit note flags he is racing at the limit of his natural role at this trip and carry of 132lbs in a competitive handicap is a test.

runners_data.name: Cloudy Rose
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old prominent-styled mare with a workmanlike record — two wins from 15 similar-going runs — who is most likely to press Clipsham Noble for the lead and may be doing so without the pace to sustain it to the line; Tom Marquand's booking elevates her tactical interest even if raw form is moderate.

runners_data.name: Yakhabar
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse by nature but mapped forward here because the field is overloaded with closers; Billy Garritty's booking and Liam Bailey's recent 2/14 form (best trainer strike rate in the race) add interest, and his win at 12f on Good is a form pointer, though his preferred rear-tracking style will be compromised if he cannot settle mid-division.

runners_data.name: Regal Glory
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good ground and placed at 14f — the trip is fine — but has struggled in 16f Soft-ground company recently; Roger Fell's 3/11 14-day record is the joint-best trainer angle in this race, and Cian Horgan's conditional claim helps, though this horse's natural back-of-the-field style is difficult to deliver when the pace is modest.

runners_data.name: Princess Vivi
runners_data.note: All her recent form has been over 7-12f, making today's 14f a step up in trip; visor fitted and her best effort was a 2nd at 8f on Good — the combination of an unproven distance and a natural hold-up style that will be squeezed by the field's composition makes her profile difficult to endorse here.

runners_data.name: Apache Eagle
runners_data.note: Ran just eight days ago and has a U (unseated) on his form string; his true style is hold-up but he is placed mid-pack by necessity, and three placed efforts from 15 similar-going runs (0 wins) suggests he is a consistent finisher without a winning turn of foot — the very short turnaround and Jessica Bedi's 0/6 recent record temper enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Coverbridge
runners_data.note: A four-year-old who has raced at distances from 7f to 14f with modest results — best effort a 3rd over 12f on Good — and Ben Ffrench Davis (5lb claimer) lightens the burden slightly; the horse's natural inclination to come from off the pace will be difficult to convert into a win when the race is unlikely to be truly run.

runners_data.name: Muhib
runners_data.note: The most consistent form horse in the race with four placings from four similar-going runs at 12-14f — three 3rds and a 4th — and Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim keeps the weight manageable; Muhib's pattern of running into the places without winning suggests he finds a gear but not enough of one, and today's controlled pace may not stretch the field sufficiently to deliver even that.

races.paceDynamic: Clipsham Noble is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 1m4f handicap and should stride into an uncontested lead from the off, setting a sustainable gallop on Good ground with no rival likely to challenge for that position. The remainder of the field — Dubai Venture, Lednikov, Jedhi Knight, Yakhabar, Regal Glory, Princess Vivi, Apache Eagle, Coverbridge and Muhib — are all hold-up types by nature, with Cloudy Rose the only other prominent-styled runner to offer any company, meaning the pace is structurally thin and unlikely to be pressured into a genuinely strong gallop. This field contains significantly more true hold-up horses than the pace map can accommodate at the rear: Yakhabar, Regal Glory, Princess Vivi, Apache Eagle, Coverbridge and Muhib are all genuine closers, and with so many needing a target to aim at, several will be forced into a midfield role they don't naturally occupy — Yakhabar and Regal Glory, with the strongest recent form and shrewd jockey bookings, are most likely to actually secure a forward position from that group. A lone front-runner setting a controlled pace on a sound surface at Pontefract — a course that rewards prominent racers who save ground on the bend — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or at least in the first half of the field and attack from two furlongs out rather than those relying on a strong pace to set up a late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Clipsham Noble Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Clipsham Noble leads uncontested and Cloudy Rose settles in second, creating a steady, controlled tempo that suits those travelling just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Clipsham Noble dictates every yard at a comfortable clip, and the horses best placed to exploit the lack of pace are those sitting second or third who can quicken into the straight at Pontefract's long home turn; hold-up types face a wall of slow-moving rivals ahead of them and cannot generate the momentum they need.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle Early
scenarios.trigger: If Cloudy Rose disputes the lead aggressively and forces Clipsham Noble to work harder than expected in the first half of the race.
scenarios.body: A genuine two-horse tussle for the front sets a more honest gallop that stretches the field and leaves those front two vulnerable late, opening the door for a hold-up horse who has settled just behind the duel and travels sweetly into contention.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the field bunches and a true closer manages to find a clear run through tiring rivals in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Pontefract's uphill finish can expose front-runners who have used themselves up, and a hold-up horse who has been shuffled along into midfield but kept fresh could produce a telling late rattle; this scenario requires a better gallop than Clipsham Noble alone is likely to generate, making it the least structurally supported shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens; Chaos Ensues
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses — among them Yakhabar or Regal Glory — try to assert their preferred forward position early, creating a scrappy, high-tempo first half.
scenarios.body: The unusually competitive early jostling for position burns energy and leaves the field strung out, benefiting a horse who dropped out quietly and finds the pace actually strong enough to deliver a genuine finish; this scenario is undercut by the fact that most of the perceived challengers for prominent spots are redistributed hold-up types who may lack the tactical speed to sustain that position.

watchPoints.text: Clipsham Noble (Liam Wright) — watch whether he is allowed to bowl along at his own pace unchallenged; if he dictates a loose lead, the race shape is entirely his to set and those hunting him from behind will need to work much harder than expected.

Yakhabar (Billy Garritty) — monitor in the parade and early stages; if Bailey's runner is sent forward aggressively to claim a forward berth rather than settling at the rear, it disrupts the assumed race shape and could force a genuine pace battle.

Cloudy Rose (Tom Marquand) — watch Marquand's intent leaving the stalls; if he pushes up to press Clipsham Noble, the gallop quickens meaningfully and changes which profile benefits, making the scenario-B closers more dangerous.

Regal Glory (Cian Horgan) — Roger Fell's 3/11 14-day form is the strongest trainer angle in the race; if Horgan can manoeuvre this natural hold-up horse into a midfield pitch rather than the back third, the combination of live form and handicap mark makes him a price to note.

Muhib (Warren Fentiman) — four consecutive placed runs on similar going at this trip make him the most consistent profile in the race; watch whether Fentiman can track the pace on the inner around Pontefract's long bend rather than getting boxed on the outside, as the route he takes to the straight will determine whether he hits the frame again.

races.name: Go Racing Bet With Jayne Handicap

runners_data.name: Sailthisshipalone
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won over course and distance last time out (1/8f/SOF) in form that reads better in isolation; Good ground is fine but today's likely steady tempo is the enemy — needs more pace to hunt down.|

runners_data.name: Flying Fletcher
runners_data.note: Front-of-race traveller who has placed at this course and distance on Good ground; Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim is a meaningful aid and 22 days between runs leaves him fresh enough, though recent form figures include a few disappointing efforts.|

runners_data.name: Rajapour
runners_data.note: Consistent each-way type who has placed three times in this distance and going combination, but his natural hold-up style is squeezed here — the field's hold-up bias means he cannot drop to his preferred rear position and he races in a compromised role throughout.|

runners_data.name: Harswell Ruby
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing mare with a win at this trip and a cluster of place efforts on Good ground; Roger Fell's yard is in decent nick (4/17 14-day) and she wears a hood, so she should settle and travel cleanly into a position that suits her if the pace is soft enough.|

runners_data.name: War Howl
runners_data.note: Recent form figures (990000) are dire and a BHA mark of 69 reflects the slide; a 33-day break and his true hold-up style being squeezed into midfield map position by the field's composition adds further risk — the ⚠ finish-fade flag is the telling detail.|

runners_data.name: Star Banner
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old who has placed twice in three starts, all on Good ground, giving a clean going profile; Charlie Johnston's runners are firing (5/48 14-day) and this hold-up type needs a true gallop to deliver, which this race may not provide.|

runners_data.name: Wetsand
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a patchy recent record (7787) and headgear noted; James Owen's yard is active with runners, but a consistent habit of finishing mid-division makes him dependent on a fast pace that Welbury is unlikely to supply today.|

runners_data.name: Welbury
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and the structural pivot of this race; Daniel Tudhope takes over for Edward Bethell (5/30 14-day), and Welbury's 1-2-2 sequence over this trip on Good ground gives him strong course and conditions credentials — racing in role throughout is the decisive tactical edge.|

runners_data.name: Mount King
runners_data.note: Six-year-old veteran carrying headgear, whose hold-up style is mapped out of position by the field's composition; Tim Easterby sends him out fit (16 days) and he has course form, but the STYLE_FIT discount is warranted given he cannot easily drop to the rear in this field.|

runners_data.name: Clonquest
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old whose best effort was a runner-up on this trip, and headgear (h) suggests there may be a temperament angle to manage; 88 days between runs is a significant freshness query, though the prominent tendency and light profile could suit if Welbury's pace is relaxed enough to allow a midfield hold.|

races.paceDynamic: Welbury is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the early lead, he should be able to dictate a measured, sustainable gallop around Pontefract's one-mile circuit from the off. Flying Fletcher and Harswell Ruby will press forward into prominent positions just off Welbury's shoulder, creating a small lead group that sets a controlled rather than searching tempo — on Good ground this tends to compress the field and reward those who travel well in mid-division. The honest handful of hold-up horses — Sailthisshipalone, Star Banner, Wetsand and Clonquest — will need a genuine end-to-end gallop to get their finishing kicks into play, but with only one genuine pace-setter that injection of pace may not materialise early enough. This shape strongly favours the lead and prominent profile: Welbury can control fractions, and those sitting just behind him in organised positions stand to benefit most when he kicks entering the home straight. The field carries more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Rajapour, War Howl and Mount King are natural closers redistributed into midfield on the map, and in a race with this thin pace, Welbury and Flying Fletcher are the horses most likely to actually secure their preferred early positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Welbury Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Welbury leads uncontested and sets an even, manageable tempo that keeps hold-up horses bottled up.
scenarios.body: Welbury dictates from the front with Flying Fletcher and Harswell Ruby close by, and the field never truly strings out enough to give closers a clear run at them; the race is effectively won from the front two or three positions entering the final quarter-mile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Ambush Off Steady Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that bunching allows late runners to storm through en masse in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A compressed, dawdle-paced affair suits Sailthisshipalone or Star Banner, who travel well in behind and produce a clean late surge; Good ground here keeps the surface fair for finishers but the thin pace makes this harder to execute than it sounds.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Flying Fletcher or Harswell Ruby press Welbury hard enough that the pace lifts and a two-horse duel unfolds.
scenarios.body: Increased mid-race tempo would suit those who travel powerfully in touch — Harswell Ruby's course form at this trip and Flying Fletcher's front-running tendencies make them natural participants; the winner emerges from this pair with the others failing to land a telling blow.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Runners Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If disruptions, shuffling, or a surprisingly strong gallop creates enough gaps for the natural closers to deliver their finishing runs.
scenarios.body: Rajapour and Mount King carry the hold-up style naturally but are mapped out of role here; even if the race shape improves for them, they face the headwind of racing out of position all day and their STYLE_FIT tags and recent form strings dampen confidence materially.

watchPoints.text: Welbury (Tudhope) — watch whether he is allowed to bowl along uncontested in the first two furlongs; if Tudhope chooses to sit and miss the lead, the entire race shape collapses and the pace dynamic becomes genuinely unpredictable.

Flying Fletcher (Tindall) — monitor his early movement: if the apprentice pushes forward to challenge Welbury for the lead, the tempo lifts significantly and changes the viability of Scenarios C and B at the expense of Scenario A.

Harswell Ruby (Mason) — the hood and prominent style mean she could be a factor if she travels sweetly just behind the lead; watch whether she gets a clean run on the outside or finds herself boxed behind slow movers from midfield.

War Howl (Mullen) — despite the BHA mark and modest recent form, a 33-day break and a clear pace scenario could see Mullen position him more aggressively than usual; worth monitoring early to confirm he drops away rather than features unexpectedly.

Sailthisshipalone (Hart) — the course-and-distance win flags capability, but watch whether the pace quickens enough in the final three furlongs; if it does not, Hart will have little room to manoeuvre and the hold-up style delivers nothing.

races.name: Tallbaldybloke Three Score And Ten Birthday Handicap

runners_data.name: Hover On The Wind
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer trained by Paul Midgley with a win and two places from nine runs on similar Good ground; David Nolan takes the ride and 8 days between runs suggests freshness, but a true closer at 5f Pontefract needs the pace to be honest enough to get home.|

runners_data.name: Betweenthesticks
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's six-year-old boasts outstanding similar-going figures (11/15, two wins and six places) and arrives on the back of a recent win, giving James Sullivan live claims; races in hood and naturally wants to close, but is sharp enough to track the pace if the race sets up slowly.|

runners_data.name: Storm Call
runners_data.note: Visor-wearing four-year-old for Michael & David Easterby with a Good-ground win on the board from five comparable outings; Billy Garritty rides and 15 days since last run is straightforward, though this hold-up type needs genuine gallop to fire at 5f.|

runners_data.name: Showtime Mahomes
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's seven-year-old returns from 133 days off — a significant concern — and is a true hold-up horse who finds himself displaced to midfield because of the crowded rear of the field; all five recent runs have been over 6f on Tapeta/Standard, which makes this 5f Good-ground assignment a notable style and surface shift.|

runners_data.name: Dream Deal
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's seven-year-old is the race's sole confirmed front-runner, proven at this course (won here over 5f on Good), and David Allan's booking is positive; with no rival to challenge from the gates, Dream Deal can control this entirely on their own terms — the only question is whether they have enough at the business end.|

runners_data.name: Dandy Dinmont
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's seven-year-old has two wins and three places in nine Good-ground starts and was last seen winning over 5f on Good 21 days ago; though a genuine hold-up horse pushed to a midfield mapping, that recent win at this trip shows he retains form — Rowan Scott will look to get a clear run.|

runners_data.name: Sea Her Excel
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's three-year-old filly has solid 5f Good-ground credentials (5/7 similar-going, one win two places) and is claimed by Elle-May Croot (5) for a 5lb reduction; she is a natural closer who sits further forward on the map than she would naturally race — the age allowance and course aptitude are the headline angles.|

runners_data.name: Brave Empire
runners_data.note: Jason Hart partners this Ivan Furtado five-year-old who wears hood and has struggled to convert, with five recent runs returning zero wins and zero places on similar going — a genuine hold-up type pushed into midfield on the map, but the flat form figures are a concern regardless of position.|

runners_data.name: Cheerleader
runners_data.note: Tina Jackson's four-year-old won over 5f on Good and Soft in her last five starts and has strong overall similar-ground figures (9/12, one win four places); returning after 32 days, Joanna Mason rides and she is a natural closer whose redistribution to midfield understates how far back she may actually race.|

runners_data.name: Davorge Nation
runners_data.note: Declan Carroll's three-year-old is listed as a non-runner — disregard for race-shape purposes; the noted 29-day break and mixed form string (0137-6) are moot if confirmation of withdrawal is received before the off.|

races.paceDynamic: Dream Deal is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 5f handicap at Pontefract and, crucially, faces no pressing rival to threaten that position from the gates — they will stride to the front uncontested and set a sustainable, controlled gallop on Good ground. The field behind is dominated by hold-up types: Hover On The Wind, Betweenthesticks, Storm Call, and others all want to race off the pace, meaning Dream Deal enjoys a clean lead with minimal early pressure. Several hold-up horses — Showtime Mahomes, Dandy Dinmont, Sea Her Excel, Brave Empire, Cheerleader, and Davorge Nation — have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply too many genuine back-of-the-field runners for all to find their natural position; Dream Deal and possibly Betweenthesticks (strong recent form) are most likely to actually secure their preferred spots. With one controlled pace-setter and a cluster of closers compressed into mid-division, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or track the pace in a ground-saving position, as the lone leader dictating a moderate tempo will be difficult to run down from a true hold-up berth.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dream Deal Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Deal leads uncontested and controls tempo from the front throughout, denying closers a strong enough gallop to overhaul.
scenarios.body: Dream Deal sets a comfortable, unhurried pace on Good ground at Pontefract, using the track's demanding uphill finish to sustain their effort — horses coming from deep have too much ground to make up in five furlongs when the pace is moderate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Stalkers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If one or two horses track Dream Deal in second or third and produce a well-timed challenge entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With Dream Deal's pace under control, any horse travelling smoothly just off the leader avoids the heavy early work while still being close enough to strike — Betweenthesticks and Hover On The Wind, both in decent recent form on Good ground, are best placed to execute this move.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Deal's pace is just sharp enough to stretch the field and create a fast-finishing run of clear ground for the deepest closers.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires a stronger early tempo than Dream Deal is likely to set alone, but if the opening stages are more frenetic than expected, a horse finishing powerfully from the rear could cut through — Betweenthesticks' proven Good-ground form and Storm Call's win on similar conditions make them candidates.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Early Splits Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If several of the redistributed hold-up types attempt to push forward early, creating an unexpectedly contested pace and a messy race shape.
scenarios.body: Should Showtime Mahomes, Dandy Dinmont, or Sea Her Excel break sharply and chase Dream Deal, the early tempo rises and the race becomes a scramble — this unsettles hold-up horses who need cover and benefits any runner with tactical flexibility to switch plans.

watchPoints.text: Dream Deal's unchallenged lead is the axis of this race — if David Allan elects to use Dream Deal's natural front-running speed and no rival matches strides early, monitor the winning margin rather than whether they lead; any challenge will come inside the final furlong.

Davorge Nation is listed as a non-runner — confirm with the declarations before settling on field size, as their absence removes a potential midfield mover and slightly eases congestion in the chasing pack.

Showtime Mahomes returns from 133 days off, has run exclusively on Tapeta/Standard surfaces recently, and now drops to 5f on turf — the combination of fitness doubt and significant surface/trip change makes their chance highly speculative regardless of market position.

With so many hold-up types compressed into mid-division, watch the early positions as the stalls open — if two or more of Dandy Dinmont, Sea Her Excel, or Cheerleader push forward to avoid being trapped, the effective pace could be sharper than Dream Deal alone would set, altering the entire race shape.|

Betweenthesticks' recent win and superior similar-going record (11/15) stand out among the chasers — monitor how James Sullivan positions them at the break, as tracking Dream Deal in second rather than coming from deep would materially improve their chance in a slow-pace scenario.|
